title: A person who substitutes distraction for moral reckoning keeps the guilt the distraction was meant to relieve
body:
- Encountering evidence of wrongdoing creates a choice between engaging with it or fleeing into distraction.
- Choosing immediate external action over self-reflection prevents moral reckoning from starting.
- Each subsequent distraction compounds the deferral, leaving guilt present but unprocessed.
- Because distraction shifts attention without altering moral responsibility, the guilt accumulates as debt instead of resolving.
conversion: Distraction meant to relieve guilt accumulates it as undealt moral debt
